facts.value: immediately upon separation for cause or layoff, unless a written policy extends it to the next regular payday or 15 days, whichever first
facts.summary: Montana: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due immediately upon separation for cause or layoff, unless a written policy extends it to the next regular payday or 15 days, whichever first.
facts.evidence_quote: (2) Except as provided in subsection (3), when an employee is separated for cause or laid off from employment by the employer, all the unpaid wages of the employee are due and payable immediately upon separation unless the employer has a written personnel policy governing the employment that extends the time for payment of final wages to the employee's next regular payday for the pay period or to within 15 days from the separation, whichever occurs first.

facts.value: next regular payday for that pay period or 15 days from separation, whichever occurs first
facts.summary: Montana: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due next regular payday for that pay period or 15 days from separation, whichever occurs first.
facts.evidence_quote: (1) Except as provided in subsection (2) or (3), when an employee separates from the employ of any employer, all the unpaid wages of the employee are due and payable on the next regular payday for the pay period during which the employee was separated from employment or 15 days from the date of separation from employment, whichever occurs first

facts.applies_to: As listed by U.S. DOL, page updated November 5, 2026
facts.summary: Montana basic state minimum wage listed by U.S. DOL: $10.85.
facts.evidence_quote: Businesses with gross annual sales of more than $110,000 Basic Minimum Rate (per hour): $10.85 Premium Pay After Designated Hours 1 : Weekly - 40 Businesses not covered by the Fair Labor Standards Act with gross annual sales of $110,000 or less Basic Minimum Rate (per hour): $4.00 Premium Pay After Designated Hours 1 : Weekly - 40 A business not covered by the federal Fair Labor Standards Act whose gross annual sales are $110,000 or less may pay $4.00 per hour. However, if an individual employee is producing or moving goods between states or otherwise covered by the federal Fair Labor Standard
facts.source_title: State Minimum Wage Laws (U.S. DOL Wage and Hour Division)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
facts.notes: Multiple rates listed by DOL (see quote): $10.85, $4.00 | Local (city or county) minimum wages are not included. Scheduled January 1, 2027 increases are not reflected until DOL updates the page.

facts.summary: Montana does not require reporting of independent contractors (per OCSE).

facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Child Support Services

facts.value: Within 20 days of hire or rehire
facts.summary: Montana: report a new hire within 20 days of the hire or rehire date.
facts.evidence_quote: Written reports must be submitted within 20 days of the employee's date of hire or rehire. Reports transmitted electronically or magnetically may be made by two transmissions monthly, if necessary
facts.notes: MCA 40-5-922. OCSE Montana entry (updated 09/24/2026) also says 'Within 20 days of hire date.' The OCSE Montana mailing address appears to be a data-entry error and is not published here.

facts.summary: Montana base new employer UI rate: Industry average (IndAvg).
facts.source_title: Significant Provisions of State Unemployment Insurance Laws, Effective July 2026
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration, Office of Unemployment Insurance
facts.notes: DOL footnote 3: min/max rates apply only to experience-rated employers and exclude surtaxes, surcharges and non-UI taxes. Footnote 4: new employer rate shown is the base rate; higher rates may apply by industry or other factors. DOL notes the report is not an official interpretation of state law. IndAvg means the new employer rate is the industry average rate; get the exact rate from the state agency. Rate basis: DOL base rate. It may exclude mandatory surcharges, fund-building rates and assessments; check the state agency or total_new_employer_rate where available.
